QF.id: SIA Logic Model for Social Programs_16

question.text: The Logical Framework Matrix (LFM) is typically organised as a 4x4 grid. The four COLUMNS are:

answer.text: Objectives (Project Elements) hierarchy / Indicators (OVIs) / Means of Verification / Assumptions (& Risks)

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Ch 4.5 case-study LFM and standard LFA teaching, the LFM columns are: (1) Project Elements / Objectives hierarchy [Impact / Outcomes / Outputs / Activities], (2) Indicators (OVIs), (3) Means of Verification, (4) Assumptions (including risks). The rows span the Impact-to-Activity hierarchy. This 4x4 discipline makes the matrix testable. **The Trap:** B conflates the ROWS (hierarchy) with the columns. C, D are irrelevant accounting / stakeholder groupings. **Cross-Exam Context:** LFM structure is tested across XXIII Ch 4, Ch 5, Ch 7 (SAS), and parallels audit-programme matrix design in statutory audit curricula. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Print a blank 4x4 LFM on your field laptop. For every SE engagement, re-draw their content into your blank template before fieldwork — if a cell is empty on your re-draw, the SE has a design gap.
